record.title: A compositional benchmark exposes the reuse–forgetting tradeoff in continual robot world models
record.summary: A September 18, 2026 arXiv preprint introduces a benchmark for continual world models in robot manipulation. Six simulated task curricula end with compositions of earlier action and perception primitives, separating reuse on a new task from forgetting on earlier tasks. The authors evaluate DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 with fine-tuning, replay, EWC and PackNet, plus a modular Prismatic World Model. In a diagnostic with an encoder pretrained on demonstrations from all benchmark tasks and then frozen, PWM reports mean forgetting score 3.85 and forward-transfer score 36.18 across six suites, compared with 34.97 and 38.11 for TD-MPC2 using that same encoder; lower forgetting and higher forward transfer are better. Without this privileged encoder, PWM is reported on par with TD-MPC2. The study is limited to simulation, three seeds, selected model settings, and no controlled parameter or compute budgets; it does not establish physical-robot performance.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v1 preprint defines six simulated Meta-World manipulation curricula that end with tasks recombining preceding primitives along action, perception, or both axes. It measures forward transfer on the composition task and forgetting on earlier tasks.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across six suites, the authors report that modular Prismatic World Model (PWM) with a pretrained frozen encoder has mean backward-transfer forgetting score 3.85 and forward-transfer score 36.18, compared with 34.97 and 38.11 for TD-MPC2 using the same encoder. Values are means over three seeds. The encoder was pretrained on expert demonstrations from all benchmark tasks; without this privileged encoder, PWM is reported on par with TD-MPC2.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: For DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2, author-reported results show forgetting generally worsening from action to perception to full composition; TD-MPC2’s mean forward transfer becomes negative for perception composition. These results are from simulated curricula and are not real-robot validation.

evidence_gaps.description: The benchmark and model results are author-reported; no independent replication across seeds or implementations was established.
The strongest PWM comparison uses a frozen encoder pretrained on demonstrations from all benchmark tasks, and the paper does not control parameter or compute budgets.
The benchmark is simulated; transfer to physical manipulation, sensor changes and imperfect resets remains unmeasured.

brief.importance_rationale: If the benchmark’s distinction between learning new interactions and reusing prior world-model knowledge generalizes, it could sharpen evaluation of continual robot learning and expose where perception or action composition drives forgetting. The result informs research and evaluation choices, but is limited to simulated curricula and author-run experiments.
limitations: The evaluation uses simulated curricula, online model-based RL and six Meta-World suites; no physical robot result is reported.
Only three random seeds are reported. The study tests selected model sizes and expert counts without controlled parameter or compute budgets.

The strongest modular PWM result depends on a frozen encoder pretrained on demonstrations from the full benchmark task distribution. Without that privileged setting, PWM is reported on par with TD-MPC2.
The fixed task-level router does not consistently recover reuse structure for temporal compositions; stage-adaptive routing and interactions between primitives remain open.
brief.summary: A September 18, 2026 arXiv preprint introduces a benchmark for continual world models in robot manipulation. Six simulated task curricula end with compositions of earlier action and perception primitives, separating reuse on a new task from forgetting on earlier tasks. The authors evaluate DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 with fine-tuning, replay, EWC and PackNet, plus a modular Prismatic World Model. In a diagnostic with an encoder pretrained on demonstrations from all benchmark tasks and then frozen, PWM reports mean forgetting score 3.85 and forward-transfer score 36.18 across six suites, compared with 34.97 and 38.11 for TD-MPC2 using that same encoder; lower forgetting and higher forward transfer are better. Without this privileged encoder, PWM is reported on par with TD-MPC2. The study is limited to simulation, three seeds, selected model settings, and no controlled parameter or compute budgets; it does not establish physical-robot performance.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report no conventional method that simultaneously solves reuse and forgetting. Under a frozen encoder pretrained on demonstrations from all tasks, PWM has mean BWT 3.85 and FWT 36.18 versus TD-MPC2 34.97 and 38.11 across six suites. Without that encoder condition, PWM is on par with TD-MPC2. Results average three random seeds.
technical.demonstrated_result: The primary preprint specifies the benchmark, methods, metrics, simulated evaluation and author-reported outcomes. No independent rerun or real-robot validation was established.
technical.implementation_status: Simulation benchmark and model experiments described in the preprint; no physical robot deployment evidence.
technical.mechanism: Each curriculum presents two or three primitive Meta-World tasks followed by a task that recombines them. The benchmark separates task-agnostic world-model backbone parameters from task-specific heads, then measures forward transfer on the final composition task and backward-transfer forgetting on prior tasks.
technical.regime: Six simulated Meta-World robot-manipulation curricula, with action, perception and full-composition tasks. Evaluated online model-based RL world models include DreamerV3, TD-MPC2 and modular PWM under several continual-learning methods. Reported results average three random seeds.
technical.reproducibility: The paper and project page provide benchmark definitions, metric formulas, full numerical tables and learning curves. No independent replication was established in this review.
technical.strongest_baseline: TD-MPC2 with the same pretrained frozen encoder is the direct modularity diagnostic; however, that encoder was trained on expert demonstrations from all benchmark tasks. Without this privileged condition, PWM is reported on par with TD-MPC2. Conventional baselines include DreamerV3 and TD-MPC2 using fine-tuning, experience replay, EWC and PackNet.

brief.title: A compositional benchmark exposes the reuse–forgetting tradeoff in continual robot world models
brief.why_it_matters: The benchmark makes a useful evaluation distinction explicit: rapid adaptation can reflect new learning rather than reuse of prior experience. Its simulation results suggest perception changes and full task compositions can make reuse harder, while also showing that a modular model’s apparent forgetting advantage depends on privileged encoder pretraining.
